newsitem.title: CANADA: Frost, several inches of snow hit Canada Prairies.
newsitem.headline: Frost, several inches of snow hit Canada Prairies.

text.p: Canada's Prairie grainbelt on Tuesday were blanketed by several hours of frost in all but the extreme south along the U.S. border and up to 13 cm (5.2 inches) of snow in the west, Environment Canada said.

The central and northern Prairie grainbelt saw overnight lows of -4.0 degrees Celsius since 2400 CDT/0500 GMT and the southern grainbelt, except in Manitoba which stayed above freezing, saw an overnight low of -1.0 C since 2400 CDT/0500 GMT, meteorologist Michel Bisson said.
Calgary saw 12 cm of snow overnight, Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan saw 13 cm of snow, Regina saw six cm of snow.
Manitoba was forecast to see snow Tuesday afternoon.
Manitoba should see highs of 4.0 to 8.0 C.
Saskatchewan should see highs of 0 to 5.0 C.
Alberta should see highs of 2.0 to 4.0 C.
Snow was forecast for all of the Prairies.

As of September 23, Alberta's harvest was 50 percent complete and Saskatchewan had combined 52 percent of crops. Manitoba, as of September 30, had 75 percent of crops in the bin, provincial agriculture reports said.
